Exclusive or selective distribution suits products where control or expertise matters, and a direct-only approach would not give the broad availability such goods require.
questions.hint: Frequent low-involvement purchases need maximum availability.

questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: Pinehurst Auto Parts, a fast-growing firm decides to stock its product in only one carefully chosen retailer per city in Foxbridge to maintain a premium image and tight control. Which distribution intensity is this?
questions.explanation: Exclusive distribution means granting very few outlets the right to sell a product in a given area, which supports a premium image and close control over service and presentation. Selective distribution uses a limited but greater number of outlets, while intensive distribution aims for as many outlets as possible. One retailer per city is the hallmark of exclusivity.
questions.hint: One outlet per area points to the most restrictive intensity.

questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: Highfield Pharmaceuticals, a large firm recorded cost of goods sold of $937,210 in Orchard last year and an average inventory of $126,784. What was its inventory turnover, rounded to one decimal?
questions.explanation: Inventory turnover is cost of goods sold divided by average inventory. Here $937,210 divided by $126,784 gives about 7.4 times per year. Inverting the ratio would describe how many years of inventory are held, not turnover, and multiplying by 100 would turn a count into an unrelated percentage. A higher turnover generally means goods sell quickly and inventory is managed efficiently.
questions.hint: Divide cost of goods sold by average inventory.
